definitions.gloss: kaiseki cuisine, traditional multi-course Japanese meal
definitions.explanation: An elaborate, multi-course Japanese meal characterized by meticulous preparation, seasonal ingredients, and beautiful presentation. Originally a simple meal served before tea ceremony, but now refers to high-end Japanese cuisine served in a set sequence of courses.

examples.japanese: {懐石|かいせき}{料理|りょうり}を{堪能|たんのう}した。
examples.english: I thoroughly enjoyed a kaiseki meal.

examples.japanese: {京都|きょうと}で{本格|ほんかく}{的|てき}な{懐石|かいせき}を{味|あじ}わった。
examples.english: I savored an authentic kaiseki meal in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: この{旅館|りょかん}では、{季節|きせつ}の{食材|しょくざい}を{使|つか}った{懐石|かいせき}{料理|りょうり}が{楽|たの}しめる。
examples.english: At this inn, you can enjoy kaiseki cuisine made with seasonal ingredients.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The name {懐石|かいせき} literally means "bosom stone." Zen monks would place a warm stone ({温石|おんじゃく}) inside their robes against their stomach to stave off hunger during fasting. The simple pre-tea-ceremony meal was named after this practice.

KAISEKI vs. KAISEKI:
- {懐石|かいせき}: originally the simple meal served before {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony)
- {会席|かいせき}: banquet-style Japanese cuisine, served at restaurants and gatherings

Both are read かいせき, and today the distinction has blurred. {懐石|かいせき}{料理|りょうり} and {会席|かいせき}{料理|りょうり} are often used interchangeably in modern Japanese to mean upscale multi-course Japanese dining.

TYPICAL COURSES:
- {先付|さきづけ}: appetizer
- {椀物|わんもの}: soup
- {向付|むこうづけ}: sashimi
- {焼物|やきもの}: grilled dish
- {煮物|にもの}: simmered dish
- {御飯|ごはん}: rice
- {甘味|かんみ}: dessert
